content.text:
# CLI reference

`omp` is invoked as:

```sh
omp [command] [flags] [messages...]
```

When the first non-flag argument is **not** a registered subcommand, `omp`
routes to the default [`launch`](#launch-the-default-command) command and treats
the arguments as the initial prompt. So `omp "fix the build"` launches a session
with that message, while `omp models` runs the `models` subcommand.

Runtime help is also available:

- `omp --help` lists user-facing subcommands and common launch flags.
- `omp <command> --help` prints that command's public flags and examples.

This page is the consolidated reference for the shared **launch surface** (the
flags accepted by `omp` / `omp launch`) and every top-level **subcommand**.
Per-subcommand flags (for example `omp auth-broker --json`) are documented by
each command's `--help`.

## Launch (the default command)

`omp` and `omp launch` start a coding session. Positional arguments become the
initial message(s):

```sh
# Interactive session
omp

# Interactive session with an initial prompt
omp "List all .ts files in src/"

# Attach files/images to the initial message (prefix with @)
omp @prompt.md @image.png "What color is the sky?"

# Non-interactive: process the prompt and exit (headless / print mode)
omp -p "List all .ts files in src/"

# Continue the previous session
omp --continue "What did we discuss?"
```

Argument handling:

- `@<path>` attaches a file or image to the initial message.
- Non-TTY stdin is read automatically as the initial prompt; do not add a `-`
  marker.
- `--` ends flag parsing; everything after it is literal message text, even if it
  looks like a flag.

### Launch flags

#### Session and workspace

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--cwd <dir>` | Directory to start in (overrides the launch cwd). |
| `--add-dir <dir>` | Add a workspace directory beyond the working directory (repeatable). |
| `--allow-home` | Allow starting in `~` without auto-switching to a temp dir. |
| `--profile <name>` | Use an isolated profile for auth, sessions, settings, and caches. |
| `--alias <name>` | Create a shell shortcut for the selected profile and exit. |
| `--config <file>` | Load an extra `config.yml`-style overlay for this run (repeatable). |
| `--session-dir <dir>` | Directory for session storage and lookup. |
| `--no-session` | Don't save the session (ephemeral). |

#### Session history

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--continue`, `-c` | Continue the previous session. |
| `--resume [id]`, `-r`, `--session [id]` | Resume a session by ID prefix or path, or open the picker when no value is given. |
| `--fork <session>` | Fork a saved session (by ID prefix or path) into a new session. See [session operations](./session-operations-export-share-fork-resume.md). |
| `--from-claude` | Import a Claude Code session into OMP. |
| `--from-codex` | Import a Codex session into OMP. |
| `--export <session>` | Export a session file to HTML and exit. |
| `--no-title` | Disable title auto-generation (equivalent to the `PI_NO_TITLE` [environment variable](./environment-variables.md)). |

#### Model selection

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--model <id-or-role>` | Model or configured role to use (role: `slow` or `@slow`; fuzzy model match: `opus`, `gpt-5.2`, or `openai/gpt-5.2`). |
| `--smol <id>` | Smol/fast model for lightweight tasks (or `PI_SMOL_MODEL`). |
| `--slow <id>` | Slow/reasoning model for thorough analysis (or `PI_SLOW_MODEL`). |
| `--plan <id>` | Plan model for architectural planning (or `PI_PLAN_MODEL`). |
| `--models <a,b,c>` | Comma-separated model patterns for `Ctrl+P` cycling. |
| `--provider <name>` | Provider to use (legacy; prefer `--model`). |
| `--api-key <key>` | API key (defaults to env vars). |
| `--provider-session-id <id>` | Reuse a specific provider-side session id for continuity and cache scoping. |
| `--prompt-cache-key <key>` | Override the provider prompt-cache key for this session. |
| `--service-tier <tier>` | OpenAI service tier for this session (`none` omits `service_tier`). |

See [providers](./providers.md) and [models](./models.md) for model resolution.

#### Thinking and reasoning

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--thinking <level>` | Set the thinking level: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, or `auto`. |
| `--hide-thinking` | Hide thinking blocks in TUI output (display only; does not disable model thinking). |
| `--print-thoughts` | Include thinking blocks in print-mode text output. |
| `--external-thinking` | Use a private scratchpad while disabling supported GPT/Claude/Gemini reasoning. Use at your own risk: providers have flagged this request shape as abuse. |

#### Prewalk and plan modes

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--prewalk` | Switch to a fast/cheap model at the first edit/write after the plan's todo list exists (default off; see `prewalk.enabled`). |
| `--no-prewalk` | Disable prewalk even if `prewalk.enabled` is set. |
| `--prewalk-into <id>` | Target model for prewalk (default the `smol` role). |
| `--plan-yolo` | Force read-only plan mode at start, auto-approve the plan on the model's first resolve call, then switch to `--plan-yolo-into` to implement it. |
| `--plan-yolo-into <id>` | Target model for plan-yolo execution (default the `smol` role). |

#### Tools, approvals, and runtime

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--tools <a,b,c>` | Comma-separated list of tools to enable (default: all). |
| `--no-tools` | Disable all built-in tools. |
| `--no-lsp` | Disable LSP tools, formatting, and diagnostics. |
| `--no-pty` | Disable PTY-based interactive bash execution. |
| `--approval-mode <mode>` | Override `tools.approvalMode` for this session (`always-ask`, `write`, or `yolo`). See [approval mode](./approval-mode.md). |
| `--auto-approve`, `--yolo` | Auto-approve all tool calls (skip approval prompts). |
| `--advisor` | Enable the advisor runtime (passively reviews each turn and injects notes). See [advisor / watchdog](./advisor-watchdog.md). |
| `--max-time <duration>` | Stop the session after this duration (e.g. `600`, `10m`, `1h`). |

#### Extensions, hooks, skills, and rules

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--extension <path>`, `-e <path>` | Load an extension (repeatable). See [extensions](./extensions.md). |
| `--hook <path>` | Load a hook/extension file (repeatable). See [hooks](./hooks.md). |
| `--trusted-extension <abs-path>` | Load a trusted extension from an absolute path (repeatable; cannot be combined with `--extension`/`-e`/`--hook`). |
| `--plugin-dir <dir>` | Add a local plugin directory to discovery (repeatable). |
| `--no-extensions` | Disable extension discovery (explicit `-e` paths still work). |
| `--skills <globs>` | Comma-separated glob patterns to filter [skills](./skills.md) (e.g. `git-*,docker`). |
| `--no-skills` | Disable skills discovery and loading. |
| `--no-rules` | Disable rules discovery and loading. See [context files](./context-files.md). |

#### System prompt

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--system-prompt <text\|file>` | System prompt (default: coding assistant prompt). See [system prompt customization](./system-prompt-customization.md). |
| `--append-system-prompt <text\|file>` | Append text or file contents to the system prompt. |

#### Output mode

| Flag | Description |
| --- | --- |

# CLI reference

`omp` is invoked as:

```sh
omp [command] [flags] [messages...]
```

When the first non-flag argument is **not** a registered subcommand, `omp`
routes to the default [`launch`](#launch-the-default-command) command and treats
the arguments as the initial prompt. So `omp "fix the build"` launches a session
with that message, while `omp models` runs the `models` subcommand.

Runtime help is also available:

- `omp --help` lists user-facing subcommands and common launch flags.
- `omp <command> --help` prints that command's public flags and examples.

This page is the consolidated reference for the shared **launch surface** (the
flags accepted by `omp` / `omp launch`) and every top-level **subcommand**.
Per-subcommand flags (for example `omp auth-broker --json`) are documented by
each command's `--help`.

## Launch (the default command)

`omp` and `omp launch` start a coding session. Positional arguments become the
initial message(s):

```sh
# Interactive session
omp

# Interactive session with an initial prompt
omp "List all .ts files in src/"

# Attach files/images to the initial message (prefix with @)
omp @prompt.md @image.png "What color is the sky?"

# Non-interactive: process the prompt and exit (headless / print mode)
omp -p "List all .ts files in src/"

# Continue the previous session
omp --continue "What did we discuss?"
```

Argument handling:

- `@<path>` attaches a file or image to the initial message.
- Non-TTY stdin is read automatically as the initial prompt; do not add a `-`
  marker.
- `--` ends flag parsing; everything after it is literal message text, even if it
  looks like a flag.

| `--cwd <dir>` | Directory to start in (overrides the launch cwd). |
| `--add-dir <dir>` | Add a workspace directory beyond the working directory (repeatable). |
| `--allow-home` | Allow starting in `~` without auto-switching to a temp dir. |
| `--profile <name>` | Use an isolated profile for auth, sessions, settings, and caches. |
| `--alias <name>` | Create a shell shortcut for the selected profile and exit. |
| `--config <file>` | Load an extra `config.yml`-style overlay for this run (repeatable). |
| `--session-dir <dir>` | Directory for session storage and lookup. |
| `--no-session` | Don't save the session (ephemeral). |

| `--from-claude` | Import a Claude Code session into OMP. |
| `--from-codex` | Import a Codex session into OMP. |

| `--no-title` | Disable title auto-generation (equivalent to the `PI_NO_TITLE` [environment variable](./environment-variables.md)). |

content:
<critical>
Plan mode active.
- Working tree/system read-only: NEVER create, edit, delete, or rename working-tree files; NEVER run state-changing commands (`git commit`, `npm install`, migrations) or otherwise change the system.
- `local://`: session-local planning artifacts; MAY create/update only when explicitly requested or needed for the plan; NEVER delete/rename.
- Canonical plan: MUST write `local://<slug>-plan.md`.

Implementing: write the plan `<slug>`/title, plain text, to `xd://propose` with `write`; `<slug>` MUST match `local://<slug>-plan.md`, allowed characters: letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens. User then selects an execution option; full write access restored.

NEVER ask user to exit plan mode or request approval in prose/with `ask`; approval ONLY via `xd://propose` write.
</critical>

## What a plan is

Plan: execution spec, not design doc. Approval may clear/compact the conversation; another engineer/fresh agent implements solely from the file. A competent implementer unfamiliar with the conversation MUST execute top-to-bottom with ZERO design decisions; file contains every choice.

Detail removes implementer decisions, not padding. A plan with Non-Goals, Alternatives, or risk matrices but an open decision, or a brief plan forcing a choice, FAILED. Decision-completeness > brevity.

## Plan file

Choose short kebab-case task `<slug>`; create `local://<slug>-plan.md` (e.g. `local://auth-token-refresh-plan.md`). File NEVER renamed on approval; submit this same `<slug>` to `xd://propose` for approval.

`edit`: incremental edits only. `write`: create/full replacement only. MUST record findings as learned; NEVER defer all writing to the end.
## Ground every claim

Resolve unknowns by discovery, not questions.

- Discoverable facts — locations, behavior, signatures, configs: MUST discover with `glob`, `grep`, `read`, or parallel `scout` subagents (via `task`). Every asserted path, symbol, signature, behavior: actually read this session. Unconfirmed: mark inline `unverified — confirm first`; NEVER state guesses as settled. Ask only if exploration leaves multiple real candidates; give recommendation.
- Preferences/tradeoffs — intent, UX, scope edges, performance vs. simplicity: not code-derivable. Ask early via `ask`: 2–4 mutually exclusive options + recommended default. Unanswered → use default; record under Assumptions.

Every question MUST alter plan or resolve load-bearing choice; batch. NEVER ask what exploration answers or filler.
## Workflow — parallel

<procedure>
1. **Understand** — request and supporting code. Scope spans areas → parallel `scout` subagents via `task`, distinct focuses: implementations, related components, test patterns. Find reusable code before proposing new.
2. **Design** — draft approach from findings, briefly weigh tradeoffs, commit. Large/cross-cutting → MAY spawn critique subagent before commitment.
3. **Review** — read intended files; validate approach against code and literal request; `ask` resolves remaining preferences.
4. **Write** — plan per **Plan contents**.
</procedure>

## Plan contents

Scannable markdown; depth follows change: one-file fix → few bullets; cross-cutting change → ordered behavior steps.

- **Context** — literal ask, need, intended end state; 2–4 sentences. Every requested outcome maps to a step; add nothing beyond ask.
- **Approach** — load-bearing ordered change steps. Order for a building tree and passing existing tests after each; state dependencies and independencies. Group by behavior, NEVER file. Each step:
  - Concrete edit: verb, exact target, new behavior; NEVER merely area to “update”/“handle”.
  - Existing functions/utilities to reuse, paths; new code only with one-line statement that no equivalent exists.
  - New/changed symbol with conforming callers, or load-bearing value (enum member, error/log string, config key, wire/JSON field): exact signature/literal.
  - Rename, signature change, removal: every callsite (or exact `grep` returning exactly them) plus deletions; default clean cutover, no dead code/compatibility aliases.
  - Rival patterns: copy and avoid named.
  - Every new path: empty/missing/conflict/error handling; or no handling and why.
- **Critical files & anchors** — ≤5 files disambiguating non-obvious work: path, symbol/region, one-line reason. Line numbers hints; implementer rereads before edit. Omit Approach-obvious files.
- **Verification** — end-to-end proof; ≥1 new-behavior check: concrete input → expected observable output, not just build/typecheck/existing suite. Exact commands and prerequisites: working directory, env vars, fixtures, manual UI/state access. Tie risky-step checks to steps.
- **Assumptions & contingencies** — only user-overridable decisions. NEVER put implementer decisions here; they belong in Approach. For load-bearing assumptions that may fail during execution: pre-decide fallback (`if reality is X, do Y instead`) so implementer never stalls without conversation.

Cut decision-free material: restated invariants, unaffected behavior, mechanical repetition, narration. Specify what implementer would otherwise invent.

<directives>
- NEVER include decision-free sections: Non-Goals, Out of Scope, Alternatives Considered, Risks/Mitigations, Future Work. Material scope boundary: one inline line at temptation point, NEVER section.
- NEVER plan mechanical cleanup tail: changelog/release notes, doc updates, formatter/linter runs, scaffold removal. These run automatically after working change; no planning. Behavior-defining tests/end-to-end proof are not cleanup: retain in **Verification**.
- NEVER reference planning conversation (`the option we chose above`, `as discussed`); unavailable to reader. State choice/reason inline.
- NEVER invent request-unspecified schema, precedence, fallback policy, unless needed to prevent concrete implementation mistake; then state decision, not open question.
</directives>

<caution>
Review options:
- **Approve and execute** — fresh context (session cleared).
- **Approve and compact context** — discussion distilled, then executes here.
- **Approve and keep context** — executes here with exploration history.
- **Save and quit** — copies the plan to a chosen path, then starts a new session.

All require self-contained file.
</caution>

<critical>
Before approval: engineer unfamiliar with conversation can execute every step without design decision and determine success at each step. Otherwise deepen any choice-forcing or ambiguous-done step.

Turn ends ONLY:
1. `ask` gathers requirements/chooses approaches; OR
2. `write` writes plan `<slug>`/title as plain text to `xd://propose` (`local://<slug>-plan.md` slug).

NEVER request plan approval via prose/`ask`; MUST use `xd://propose` write. MUST continue until decision-complete.
</critical>

content.text: Loading a new session still takes forever, is it possible to thing of a way to speed things up using agents for loading a new section ( especially the learn and review, is review in all the modes now btw?)

content.thinking:
The user asks two things:
1. "Loading a new session still takes forever, is it possible to think of a way to speed things up using agents for loading a new section (especially the learn and review)"
2. "is review in all the modes now btw?"

I'm in plan mode: read-only for working tree, must produce a plan to `local://<slug>-plan.md` and submit via `xd://propose`. But first: understand the request. The user wants to reduce the wall-clock time of "loading a new section" — i.e. the Learn preparation flow (read pages, view pages, snapshot figures, write lesson, review crew) and review. They ask about using agents/subagents to parallelize.

Key facts I need to discover before planning:
- Where does the time go in a new Learn section? The flow: source preparation (read every page, view every page, save crops for every figure), lesson authoring in parts, coverage ledger, lessonComplete → review crew (currently sequential per packet? REVIEW_CONCURRENCY=6 parallel workers, but each worker is a separate `modelRegistry.complete` call — runReviewPass runs up to 6 packets concurrently) → commit → 3 short questions.
- What's actually slow: (a) the *authoring* loop (many turns: read page ranges one by one, view pages one by one, snapshot each figure, then write lesson units in parts), (b) the review crew (parallel already, but 3 roles each with multiple packets; each reviewer run is a full model turn loop with tool calls; with `prepared: true` it's one request per packet).
- "using agents" — in this harness, `task` subagents can be spawned by the main agent. Does the Scholar extension have any tool for spawning subagents? The extension registers the `scholar` tool only. The Pi host has a `task` tool. Could the *workflow* be changed so Scholar spawns parallel workers (e.g. Pi's task tool) for page reading / figure review? That's a real architecture question: the extension's own review layer already parallelizes reviewer calls internally (concurrency 6) — the slow part for the *author* is sequential tool calls in the main loop (read/view/snapshot/notes).

Wait — what does "loading a new session" mean exactly? Two readings:
(a) The wall-clock of starting a NEW study session on a new section (the "loading" progress widget covers exactly this: `loading-progress.ts`, and the runtime-coordinator's loading stages). The user says "Loading a new session still takes forever" and "speed things up using agents for loading a new section (especially the learn and review)".
(b) omp/pi session startup time (harness startup) — "loading a new session" as in starting the CLI. But "using agents for loading a new section" clearly points at the Scholar *section preparation* flow.

Given the guard on my last answers (loading widget, review crew, review restored), (a) is right: the Scholar "preparing this section" flow that shows the loading widget ("Scholar · reading pages…", "review · round N · 45m shared deadline").

So what can be parallelized, concretely, by reading the code:
1. **Source preparation**: the author (main model) calls `scholar` action=read (page ranges, at most 8 pages), action=view (1 page per call), action=snapshot (1 crop per call), notes.figureReviews per page. These are strictly sequential tool calls in one model loop → N pages = N view calls + reads + snapshots. This is the biggest wall-clock sink for a long section.
   - Could the extension parallelize these internally? No — the model drives them one at a time.
   - Could the *model* spawn subagents (Pi's `task` tool) to read/view pages in parallel? The subagent would need access to the scholar tool with the right activation/authority — the extension's controller is per-session with activation state; a subagent runs a separate session (different agent) — the docs say subagents run headless with their own runtime; they'd have the `task` tool surface... The `scholar` tool requires an active Learn activation bound to the coordinator... Subagents likely can't drive the interactive session's tool.
   - But: NOT every page needs the *model's eyes*. `view` renders a page image for the model to inspect — required by `assertLearnFigureCoverage` (every page read AND viewed before practice; figure reviews per page). The model must see pages to write the lesson; that's inherent.
   - However, omp/pi has `task` with a `vision`-capable subagent? The `task` tool spawns agents with the same toolset. If Scholar allowed *delegated* page inspection: e.g. a scholar action that returns multiple rendered pages in one call (batch view). Actually `read` supports ranges (up to 8 pages). `view` is 1 page/call. Could `scholar` view multiple pages in one call? That's a code change: `handleSourceView` accepts one page. A batched `view` (e.g. `pages: [1,2,3]`) would collapse N round trips into one — big win, no agents needed.
   - Similarly `snapshot` is one crop per call; a batch snapshot (multiple rectangles in one call) would help.

2. **Review crew**: already parallel (REVIEW_CONCURRENCY 6, one request per packet). Remaining slowness: (i) `reviewLearnDraft` runs the three ROLES *sequentially*? Let me check: `reviewLearnDraft` iterates roles sequentially ("for (const role of roles)") and each role runs its packets in parallel. For a big section: source role = up to 8 pages / 4 pages per packet; teaching = #topics; visual = pages+crops. AggregateReviews per role. If roles run sequentially, that's 3 waves (each wave parallel within role) — an easy win: run roles concurrently (they're independent: source/teaching/visual each with their own packets and evidence).
   - (ii) The visual role with a vision model renders pages — expensive but parallelizable.
   - So: parallelize roles (concurrency budget already 6).

3. **Checkpoint reuse** already avoids re-running.

4. Also: the *loading widget* shows rounds; the user's "takes forever" may include the author's sequential authoring turns (which are model-bound, not scheduler-bound).

The user asks "is it possible to think of a way to speed things up using agents" — I should propose concrete mechanisms that fit this repo's architecture:
- The extension cannot spawn Pi subagents (no access to `task`), but it CAN:
  (a) run its existing reviewer crew with **per-role** concurrency (roles in parallel) instead of per-role sequential waves,
  (b) **batch** source-preparation calls (multi-page view, multi-crop snapshot) to collapse round trips,
  (c) **pipeline** preparation: start review work as soon as a topic's material is ready? (harder, changes semantics)
  (d) increase REVIEW_CONCURRENCY? The worker count is 6; each worker = one model request. The provider rate limits matter.

Hmm — but also the *real* answer to "using agents": in this harness the *author* model could use the `task` tool to parallelize page digestion... but Scholar's invariants require the *authoring* model to produce the lesson; subagents lack the scholar tool/activation. Let me verify whether the scholar tool is available to subagents: subagents have their own toolset; extension tools registered by the extension are host-level so a headless subagent probably *does* get the `scholar` tool but with a *different* coordinator/session? Actually the coordinator is created per extension load in the host process; a subagent spawns a new agent... in pi, `task` subagents run in the same process? The docs: `task` spawns subagents with full capabilities; the extension's `pi.on("tool_call")` hooks are registered per extension instance in the host. If subagents share the extension instance, their scholar calls would hit the same session state (activation bound to the parent session) — could work but would serialize on the mutation queue and risk authority checks (session.state). Uncertain — and risky.

So the *safe, high-value* plan: make the **extension-side** work concurrent and batched:
1. Review crew: run all roles concurrently in one wave (bounded by REVIEW_CONCURRENCY), so a 3-role review takes max(packets in role) instead of sum(role waves).
2. Batch page rendering: allow `action: "view"` with multiple pages (`pages: [..]`) returning all images in one result — cut N round trips to 1. Must keep the existing receipt semantics (`sourceFigureViews` per page, freshness assertions per page).

# Learn-section round-trip quantification (repo C:\\Users\\basam\\.pi\\agent\\extensions\\scholar)

## 1. The Learn-mode contract in policies.ts (learnInstructions, lines 71-115)

Required scholar calls, in the order the contract demands (quotes verbatim, citations are the bullet line numbers):

1. **Read the whole section** — line 100: `- Read the complete active section range before claiming coverage. Extract the primary claims, definitions, mechanisms, procedures, examples, equations, boundary conditions, figures, and misconceptions needed to substitute for reading.`
2. **Save the plan (objectives + sourceCoverage) before drafting** — line 102: `- Save the plan before drafting a long lesson: action=notes with top-level objectives and sourceCoverage (without lesson evidence yet). figureReviews, objectiveChecks, synthesis and keyPoints may each be saved independently; do not regenerate prose just to update metadata.` and its tail `Use action=status to inspect persisted work;`
3. **Read AND view every page, crop every figure, then record figureReviews** — line 103 (the per-page/per-figure bullet): `- During initial source preparation, before the first practice or mastery question, read and view every active-section page. Save a tight literal crop of every source figure, graph, table, map, or diagram by default, including vector diagrams whose captions are absent from extracted text. Use the snapshotId returned by snapshot to account for each visual in notes.figureReviews; each page needs a visual observation and its figures list.` … `Skip only genuinely decorative, duplicate, or fully redundant visuals, with a specific skipReason; an empty figures list means visual inspection found none belonging to this section.`
4. **Save the explanation as lesson units** — line 105: `- Save each actual explanation explicitly with scholar action=notes and lesson={id,title,markdown,objectives,keyPoints,sourcePages}. Use a stable id for identical retries; to revise after review, first read status with lessonId and include its current expectedContentHash;` (line 104 adds `Save the lesson in readable topical units`).
5. **Repair loop** — line 106: `- For a targeted repair, use notes.lessonPatch with the current id/expectedContentHash from status.` and line 107: `Complete the source-grounded explanations of every objective and essential equation/figure, perform the focused editorial review, and save repairs before setting notes.lessonComplete=true. … Read their concrete findings, repair the affected passages with the current expectedContentHash, update the checklist's exact evidence and resubmit.`
6. **Completion gate** — line 107 again (`notes.lessonComplete=true`); line 108 forbids automatic retry after an execution failure.
7. **3 mastery questions** — line 109: `- After the lesson is saved, ask exactly 3 short questions, one at a time, with grounding purpose=mastery.`

Per-page / per-figure work is imposed by exactly two bullets: line 100 (read the whole range) and line 103 (`read and view every active-section page`, `Save a tight literal crop of every source figure … by default`, `each page needs a visual observation and its figures list`).

## 2. Accepted parameters and hard limits per action

| action | parameters | limit (literal constant / check) | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read` | startPage, endPage, maxChars | `export const MAX_TOOL_PAGES = 12;` → `if (end - start + 1 > MAX_TOOL_PAGES) throw new Error(\`Scholar read accepts at most ${MAX_TOOL_PAGES} pages per call.\`)`; `MAX_TOOL_CHARS = 60_000`; default `Math.min(params.maxChars || 40_000, MAX_TOOL_CHARS)`; a truncated Learn excerpt is rejected outright | tool-contract.ts:6,7; tool-actions/source.ts:23,51,61 |
| `view` | page | exactly one page: `if (!page) throw new Error("Scholar view requires page.")`; scope assert `(…, page, page)`; `renderPdfPage(book, page)`; schema field is a single `page: Type.Optional(Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 }))` | tool-actions/source.ts:98-100; tool-contract.ts:141 |
| `snapshot` | page, x, y, width, height, canvasWidth, canvasHeight, caption | one rectangle per call: `if (coordinates.some((value) => value === undefined)) throw new Error("Scholar snapshot requires x, y, width, height, canvasWidth, and canvasHeight from a prior view call.")`; schema bounds `x,y ≤ 20_000`, `width,height ∈ [32, 20_000]`; caption ≤ 500 chars | tool-actions/visuals.ts:74-75,95; tool-contract.ts:142-148 |
| `search` | query, limit | `searchSource(book, params.query, params.limit || 8, ranges)` (default 8 hits); schema `limit: Type.Optional(Type.Integer({ minimum: 1, maximum: 20 }))` | tool-actions/source.ts:145; tool-contract.ts:152 |
| `image_search` | query, limit | `searchCommonsImages(query, Math.min(limitParam || 3, 4), signal)` → at most 4 candidates per call regardless of `limit`; Exam/Tutor only (`setCache({ mode: session.mode as "exam" | "tutor" …})`) | tool-actions/visuals.ts:233,239-244 |
| `image_save` | imagePageId, caption | one candidate per call, and only from the latest `image_search` in the same active Exam/Tutor record: `if (!imageSearchCache || imageSearchCache.bookId !== book.id || … || !imageSearchCache.pageIds.has(pageId)) throw new Error("Scholar image_save accepts only a candidate from the latest image_search in this active Exam or Tutor record.")`; caption ≤ 500 | tool-actions/visuals.ts:290-298,301 |

## 3. What `assertLearnFigureCoverage` requires (figure-coverage.ts)

Per page in `[section.startPage, section.endPage]`:
- a read receipt — `entry.read = true` (recordLearnRead) — figure-coverage.ts:101, required by `pendingFigurePages` scanning `for (let page = section.startPage; page <= section.endPage; page++)` and checking `!entry?.read || !entry.viewed || !entry.review` — figure-coverage.ts:175-184.
- a view receipt — `entry.viewed = { width, height }` — figure-coverage.ts:116, same requirement at 178-183.
- a figure review with an observation — `if (typeof review.observation !== "string")` / `observation.length < 12 || observation.length > 500 … throw` — figure-coverage.ts:141-144 (`Read and view PDF page ${page} before recording its figure review.`).
- every caption candidate accounted for — `const missing = entry.candidates.filter((label) => !labels.has(label)); if (missing.length) throw` — figure-coverage.ts:160-161.
Per figure:
- a distinct label plus exactly one of `snapshotId` or `skipReason` — `Boolean(snapshotId) === Boolean(skipReason)` throws — figure-coverage.ts:150-156; a skip must be justified in 20-500 chars (156).
- the snapshot must exist for that page and match its stored sha256 — verifySnapshot, `Figure coverage needs a saved snapshot from page ${page}: ${snapshotId}.` / `no longer matches its source snapshot` — figure-coverage.ts:119-128, called at 157 and re-verified for every reviewed figure in `assertLearnFigureCoverage` (185-192).
- the error text itself states the per-figure default: `save every useful source visual, then record notes.figureReviews with saved snapshot IDs or specific justified skips. Include vector diagrams even when text extraction found no caption.` — figure-coverage.ts:187.
Gate call sites: every non-diagnostic Learn question (index.ts:345, 371), every Learn assessment (tool-controller.ts:824, 828), every lesson completion/commit (tool-controller.ts:686, 768, 790).

## 4. Minimum model turns / calls for N pages, F figures, T topics

Assume the author follows the instruction text literally and each row is one call (schema-permitted combinations noted).

| step | call | count for N pages / F figures / T topics | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Read source | `scholar action=read` | ⌈N/12⌉ (12 pages/call cap; the 40k-char default and the Learn truncation-throw can force more, smaller reads) | tool-contract.ts:6; tool-actions/source.ts:23,51,61 |
| 2 View each page | `action=view` | N (exactly one page per call) | tool-actions/source.ts:98-100; tool-contract.ts:141; figure-coverage.ts:178-183 |
| 3 Crop each figure | `action=snapshot` | F (one rectangle per call) | tool-actions/visuals.ts:74-75,96-115; tool-contract.ts:142-147 |
| 4 Figure inventory | `notes.figureReviews` | 1 (one array carries all pages: `maxItems: 200`, capped at the section's page count by `reviews.length > section.endPage - section.startPage + 1`) | tool-contract.ts:191; figure-coverage.ts:131-132,141-161 |
| 5 Plan | `notes {objectives, sourceCoverage}` | 1 | policies.ts:102; tool-contract.ts:164,166; tool-actions/learning.ts (objectives must be declared or "Nothing saved") |
| 6 Recap + key points | `notes {synthesis, keyPoints}` | 1 | policies.ts:102,165; lesson.ts:344 (`!section.synthesis?.trim() || !section.keyPoints.length → "save a recap and key points"`) |
| 7 Check plan | `notes {objectiveChecks}` | 1 | policies.ts:102; tool-contract.ts:188 |
| 8 Lesson | `notes {lesson}` | 1 minimum (all T topics live as `###` headings inside one unit — `splitTopics` splits one lesson entry into topics) up to T if the author saves one unit per topic | tool-contract.ts:170-179; learn-review.ts:75-76; policies.ts:104-105 |
| 9 Commit | `notes {lessonComplete:true}` | 1 (may ride the same call as step 8) | tool-contract.ts:180; tool-controller.ts:749-797 |
| 10 Post-review repair | `action=status` then `notes {lessonPatch, coverageUpdates, findingResponses, lessonComplete}` | ≥1 status + ≥1 combined call; up to 4 pre-review rejections allowed | policies.ts:105-107; tool-contract.ts:181-187,167-169; tool-controller.ts:86 (`MAX_PREREVIEW_REJECTIONS = 4`) |
| 11 Mastery checks | `scholar_quiz` (one per question, one at a time) | 3 | policies.ts:109; quiz.ts:509-511 |

**Arithmetic (literal, one call per named step, one lesson unit holding all T topics):**

```
total = ceil(N/12) + N + F + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + (1 status + 1 repair) + 3
      = ceil(N/12) + N + F + 12
```

**Arithmetic (minimum, using the schema's permission to combine notes fields):** the plan must be saved before the lesson (policies.ts:102), so at least 2 notes calls before the first commit (plan; then everything else incl. `figureReviews` + `objectiveChecks` + `synthesis` + `keyPoints` + `lesson` + `lessonComplete` in one call), plus status + one repair resubmission, plus 3 quizzes:

```
total_min = ceil(N/12) + N + F + 2 + 1 + 1 + 3 = ceil(N/12) + N + F + 7
```

Worked example, N=20, F=6, T=5: reads ⌈20/12⌉=2, views 20, snapshots 6 → 2+20+6+7 = **35 calls minimum**, 43 under the literal one-note-call-per-step / one-lesson-unit-per-topic reading.

**Model turns vs tool calls.** Pi executes sibling tool calls from a single assistant message concurrently (`extensions.md:784`: "In the default parallel tool execution mode, sibling tool calls from the same assistant message are preflighted sequentially, then executed concurrently"; also `extensions.md:1925`: "tool calls run in parallel by default"). So the dependency DAG — reads and views are independent, each snapshot depends only on its own page's view — collapses to roughly: 1 turn of all reads + all views, 1 turn of all snapshots, 1 plan turn, 1 lesson turn, 1 commit turn, 1 status/repair turn, 3 question turns ≈ **9-10 turns** regardless of N/F. [INFERENCE: the batching is the model's choice; the host capability is cited, the author model's willingness to emit N sibling calls is UNCONFIRMED.] The binding constraint is context, not the tool API: the reviewer path caps images at 24 per request (`review-runtime.ts:58 maxImages: 24`).

**Review work is not author work.** `notes.lessonComplete=true` triggers `reviewLearnDraft` inside the extension (tool-controller.ts:785), which fans out reviewer packets — ⌈N/4⌉ source windows (`SOURCE_WINDOW_PAGES = 4`, learn-review.ts:62,97-99), T teaching checks + 1 coherence check, and visual packets bundling up to 6 images (`VISUAL_PACKET_IMAGES = 6`, learn-review.ts:63) — executed 6-at-a-time (`REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6`, review-layer.ts:76; worker pool `await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, packets.length) }, worker))`, review-layer.ts:513). Tests confirm this: `assert.equal(captures.length, 4, "one source window, one topic check, one coherence check and one visual packet")` (tests/verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs:94) and 11 pages → reads `[[1,1],[1,4],[5,8],[9,11]]` (line 330). These are parallel model requests already; they add reviewer turns, not author turns.

## 5. Places where one call already covers many pages/figures (do not invent new batching)

- **read** already batches 12 pages: `MAX_TOOL_PAGES = 12` (tool-contract.ts:6), enforced at tool-actions/source.ts:23, with one receipt write covering the whole range (`recordLearnRead(book, section, source, start, end)` iterates `extractedPages(source, start, end)`, figure-coverage.ts:92-107).
- **figureReviews** already covers every page and figure in one call (tool-contract.ts:191 `maxItems: 200`; figure-coverage.ts:132 caps at the section's page count, i.e. all of them).
- **coverageUpdates** already covers the whole checklist in one call: `maxItems: 200` (tool-contract.ts:167-169).
- **lessonPatch** already covers up to 16 edits/callout replacements in one call (tool-contract.ts:183-185).
- **search** returns up to 20 hits per call (tool-contract.ts:152; default 8 at tool-actions/source.ts:145).
- **Review crew** is already bulk: 4-page source windows, one check per topic, 6 images per visual packet, 6 concurrent reviewers (learn-review.ts:62-63; review-layer.ts:76,513); each reviewer reads 8 pages per call (`read_source` … `if (end < start || end - start > 7) throw new Error("Read one to eight consecutive pages.")`, review-layer.ts:241-248).
- The only genuinely one-unit-per-call steps are **view** (single page) and **snapshot** (single rectangle).

## Host-SDK capability notes for the goal decision (pi 0.85.1)

- Extensions can already issue parallel model requests: this repo does it by building a `Context` and calling the provider directly — `modelRegistry: Pick<ExtensionContext["modelRegistry"], "complete"> & Partial<Pick<…, "getProvider" | "getApiKeyAndHeaders">>` (review-runtime.ts:70) and `const provider = options.modelRegistry.getProvider!(options.model.provider); … provider.streamSimple(requestModel, context, {...})` (review-runtime.ts:307-316), with cancellation one turn later (`cleanupSessionResources`, review-runtime.ts:467).
- The extension context surface exposes `modelRegistry`, `model`, `scopedModels`, `thinkingLevel`, `signal` (dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:209-233; documented at docs/extensions.md:1013-1016).
- Pi already runs sibling tool calls concurrently by default (docs/extensions.md:784, 1925) — so parallelizing reads/views/snapshots needs no host change, only an authoring pattern.
- "Subagents" in this SDK are not an ExtensionContext primitive: the documented pattern is `createAgentSession` from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (docs/sdk.md:19-24, 46-61) or spawning a separate `pi` process — the shipped example says `Spawns a separate pi process for each subagent invocation, giving it an isolated context window` and uses `spawn` from `node:child_process` (examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:4-5,15,345-349; the extensions feature table lists `subagent/` as `Spawn sub-agents | registerTool, exec`, docs/extensions.md:3005). None of the scholar tool actions currently spawn subagents; its parallel review crew is the in-process equivalent.

## Verification note
All limits, schemas and requirements above were read from the source files listed (tool-contract.ts, tool-actions/source.ts, tool-actions/visuals.ts, figure-coverage.ts, learn-review.ts, review-layer.ts, review-runtime.ts, tool-controller.ts, policies.ts) and from the installed SDK docs/types; no repo documentation file was used as evidence.

# Findings — pi 0.85.1 extension capabilities (SDK root: `C:/Users/basam/AppData/Local/pi-node/current/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`)

## 1. What `ExtensionAPI` exposes

Full interface: `dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:906` → `1084`.
```ts
export interface ExtensionAPI {
    on(event: "project_trust", handler: ProjectTrustHandler): void;   // 907
export interface ExtensionAPI {                                        // 906
    /** Shared event bus for extension communication. */
    events: EventBus;                                                  // 1082-1083
```

**(a) spawn a subagent / task — NONE.** No member named `spawn*`, `task`, `agent(s)`, `runTask`, `createSession*`. The only process/command entry point is:
```ts
    /** Execute a shell command. */
    exec(command: string, args: string[], options?: ExecOptions): Promise<ExecResult>;   // types.d.ts:992-993
```
with `ExecOptions = { signal?: AbortSignal; timeout?: number; cwd?: string }` (`dist/core/exec.d.ts:8-14`). Everything else process-related is raw `node:child_process` imported by the extension itself (as the example does, `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:15` → `import { spawn } from "node:child_process";`). Session lifecycle members exist only on `ExtensionCommandContext` (`newSession`/`fork`/`switchSession`/`navigateTree`, types.d.ts:264-293) or on `ReplacedSessionContext` (`sendMessage`/`sendUserMessage`, types.d.ts:297-305) — they replace *the current* session, they do not create parallel workers.

**(b) invoke a tool — no direct invocation API.** There is registration and tool-name bookkeeping only:
```ts
    /** Register a tool that the LLM can call. */
    registerTool<TParams extends TSchema = TSchema, TDetails = unknown, TState = any>(tool: ToolDefinition<TParams, TDetails, TState>): void;  // 943-944
    getActiveTools(): string[]; getActiveTools(): string[];                 // 994-995
    getAllTools(): ToolInfo[]; setActiveTools(toolNames: string[]): void;   // 996-998
```
Tool *interception* is possible via `on("tool_call")` / `on("tool_result")` / `on("tool_execution_*")` (types.d.ts:937-942), but no `callTool()` exists — an extension can only call its own code, `pi.exec`, or (for the LLM) `sendUserMessage`/`sendMessage` (types.d.ts:971-983).

**(c) call a model — only through the context registry, not via `ExtensionAPI`.**
```ts
    setModel(model: Model<any>): Promise<boolean>;                          // 1005-1006
    registerProvider(provider: Provider): void;                              // 1066
    registerProvider(name: string, config: ProviderConfig): void;            // 1067
```
Actual generation uses `ExtensionContext.modelRegistry` (`types.d.ts:220-221`: `modelRegistry: ModelRegistry;`), i.e. `ModelRegistry.complete(model, context, options): Promise<AssistantMessage>` (`dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:31`), documented as *"Synchronous compatibility facade exposed to extensions"* (`dist/core/model-registry.d.ts:19`). No `pi.complete(...)` shortcut exists.

**(d) parallel / background work — nothing built in.** No timer, worker, queue, or scheduler member. The only "fire and forget" member is:
```ts
    /** Trigger compaction without awaiting completion. */
    compact(options?: CompactOptions): void;                                // types.d.ts:245-246
```
Parallelism therefore comes from plain JS (`Promise.all` in your own code) and from the harness's own tool fan-out (`docs/extensions.md:784`: "In the default parallel tool execution mode, sibling tool calls from the same assistant message are preflighted sequentially, then executed concurrently"). Per-tool opt-in/out is `ToolDefinition.executionMode?: "sequential" | "parallel"` (`types.d.ts:361-364`; declared in pi-agent-core `dist/types.d.ts:22`).

**(e) extension state shared across sessions.** Nothing session-transcending is *provided*; what exists is:
```ts
    /** Append a custom entry to the session for state persistence (not sent to LLM). */
    appendEntry<T = unknown>(customType: string, data?: T): void;           // 984-985
    events: EventBus;                                                        // 1082-1083
```
`appendEntry` writes into the *current* session file (per-session). `events` is `{ emit(channel, data); on(channel, handler) }` (`dist/core/event-bus.d.ts:1-3`) — in-process, per event-bus instance, shared between the extensions loaded into one runtime. Cross-session sharing is only whatever your module-level variables hold (see Q4 for lifetime) or what you persist yourself (Scholar: Obsidian/state files).

## 2. Subagent / agent-spawning capability reachable from an extension

**None exists in the API.** Exhaustive grep of `dist/**` for `subagent|sub-agent|spawnAgent|runTask|TaskTool` returns matches only in `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `docs/*`, and `examples/**`. There is no exported symbol to quote — the nearest exported artifact is the *example* tool registration:
```ts
	pi.registerTool({
		name: "subagent",
		label: "Subagent",            // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:472-474
```
whose implementation spawns an OS process, not an in-process agent:
```ts
			const invocation = getPiInvocation(args);
			const proc = spawn(invocation.command, invocation.args, {   // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:345-346
	const args: string[] = ["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session"];    // examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:300
```
Confirmed absent at product level too: `README.md:501` — "**No sub-agents.** There's many ways to do this. Spawn pi instances via tmux, or build your own with [extensions](#extensions), or install a package that does it your way." And the built-in tool vocabulary contains no `task`:
```ts
export type ToolName = "read" | "bash" | "powershell" | "edit" | "write" | "grep" | "find" | "ls";   // dist/core/tools/index.d.ts:20
```
(grep for `name: "task"` / `"task"` across `dist/core` and `dist/bundle` → no tool definition; the only `Task`-ish hits are unrelated Anthropic SDK strings.)

Child processes *can* be pointed at specific extensions via CLI flags: `extensions?: string[]`, `noExtensions?: boolean`, `tools?: string[]` (`dist/cli/args.d.ts:27-32`).

## 3. Concurrency limit / rate limiting / queue for model requests from an extension

**Not documented and not implemented.** The call chain is a straight passthrough with no limiter:
```js
    complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.runtime.complete(model, context, options);     // dist/core/model-registry.js:65-66
```
```js
    complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.stream(model, context, options).result();      // dist/core/model-runtime.js:458-459
```
```js
    async complete(model, context, options) {
        return this.stream(model, context, options).result();      // pi-ai dist/models.js:387-388
```
`ModelRuntime.stream` just prepares auth and calls `provider.stream(...)` (`dist/core/model-runtime.js:454-457`) — no semaphore/queue/in-flight cap anywhere on that path (greps for `concurren|semaphore|Limiter|rate.?limit|maxConcurrent` over `dist/**` and over `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/**` return only retry logic, undici pool internals, and unrelated provider strings).

The only serialization present is *credential-scoped*, not request-scoped:
```js
    /** Serialize tasks per provider id without releasing the chain before active work settles. */
    enqueue(providerId, task, options) {                            // pi-ai dist/auth/credential-store.js:10-11
```
Retry is configurable but is not a rate limit:
```ts
export interface ProviderRetrySettings {
    timeoutMs?: number;
    maxRetries?: number;              // dist/core/settings-manager.d.ts:13-16
```
Docs only warn that refresh is unbounded without a signal — `docs/extensions.md:1746`: "Public `ModelRuntime.refresh()` and `ModelRegistry.refresh()` calls accept an optional signal and are unbounded when it is omitted; extensions and applications choose their own deadlines." **Conclusion: any cap (e.g. 4-6 concurrent reviews) is the extension's own responsibility** — which is exactly what Scholar already does:
```ts
export const REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6;                                  // review-layer.ts:76
  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(REVIEW_CONCURRENCY, packets.length) }, worker));   // review-layer.ts:513
      response = await abortable(
        Promise.race([options.modelRegistry.complete(options.model, context, requestOptions), stallPromise]),   // review-runtime.ts:296-297
```

## 4. Do subagents see the same extension's tools/hooks, and share module state?

**For the only subagent mechanism the SDK provides (a child `pi` process): no — nothing is shared.** Each process discovers and loads extensions itself:
```ts
export declare function discoverAndLoadExtensions(configuredPaths: string[], cwd: string, agentDir?: string, eventBus?: EventBus): Promise<LoadExtensionsResult>;   // dist/core/extensions/loader.d.ts:22
```
A child spawned with `--mode json -p --no-session` (`examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:300`) starts its own runner, its own `ExtensionContext`, its own session file, and its own module instances; the parent's registered tools are visible to it only if they also load there, or if the parent passes an explicit allowlist (`--tools ...`, `examples/extensions/subagent/index.ts:307`). The README for that example states the isolation intent: "**Isolated context**: Each subagent runs in a separate `pi` process" (`examples/extensions/subagent/README.md:7`).

**In-process nuance (partially confirmed):** if an extension instead called the SDK's `createAgentSession()` itself, the nested session gets its own `LoadExtensionsResult` (`dist/core/sdk.d.ts:48-49`, `CreateAgentSessionResult.extensionsResult`), and the resource loader uses the *cached* loader (`dist/core/resource-loader.js:412,426,441`: `loadExtensionsCached(...)`). Caching is at module level keyed by extension path + resolved cwd:
```js
        const cachedFactory = extensionCache.get(extensionPath);     // dist/core/extensions/loader.js:411
        moduleCache: false,                                          // dist/core/extensions/loader.js:417
```
```js
async function initializeExtension(factory, extensionPath, resolvedPath, cwd, eventBus, runtime) {   // loader.js:458
        await factory(load.api);                                     // loader.js:462
```
[INFERENCE] Because the *module* is evaluated once per (path, cwd generation) while the *factory* is invoked once per load, two in-process sessions would get separate `Extension` objects (separate tool/handler registries) but would share module-level mutable state of the extension file. I did not find a test or doc asserting this either way, so treat the module-state-sharing half as **unconfirmed**.

**Unconfirmed / out of scope:** the *harness* here is not pi (the `task`/`agent://` tooling referenced in this session's prompt does not exist in this SDK). I grepped `C:/Users/basam/.pi/**` for `"task"` and `name: "task"` (no matches) and grepped the whole `pi-node/current/node_modules` tree for `subagent|sub-agent|spawnAgent|runTask` (matches only inside pi-coding-agent docs/CHANGELOG/examples) and the pi-server package for `subagent|spawnAgent|name: "task"|TaskTool` (no matches). Whether the actual host harness's `task` tool propagates extension tools/state to subagent sessions therefore **could not be confirmed from the installed SDK** — the evidence points to pi 0.85.1 having no such tool at all.

## 5. `ExtensionContext`: session id, subagent detection, abort plumbing

```ts
export interface ExtensionContext {                  // dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:209
    sessionManager: ReadonlySessionManager;          // 218-219
    signal: AbortSignal | undefined;                 // 235-236
    abort(): void;                                   // 237-238
    isIdle(): boolean;                               // 231-232
    hasPendingMessages(): boolean;                   // 240
```
- **Active session id: yes, indirectly** — `ReadonlySessionManager` is `Pick<SessionManager, "getCwd" | "getSessionDir" | "getSessionId" | "getSessionFile" | ...>` (`dist/core/session-manager.d.ts:140`), with `getSessionId(): string` at line 208 and `getSessionFile(): string | undefined` at 209. Same data is exported to child shells: `env.PI_SESSION_ID = ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId();` (`dist/core/tools/bash.js:128`), and the child env is scrubbed of inherited values first (`bash.js:121-125`: `delete env.PI_SESSION_ID; ...`).
- **Subagent-vs-main detection: no.** There is no `isSubagent`/`parentSession`/agent-id member on `ExtensionContext`; the closest signals are `SessionStartEvent.reason: "startup" | "reload" | "new" | "resume" | "fork"` (`types.d.ts:404-408`) and `sessionManager.getSessionFile() === undefined` for `--no-session` children. **Explicitly unconfirmed**: nothing I read establishes an API for distinguishing a subagent run from the main run.
- **Abort plumbing a long parallel operation must respect: yes.** `ctx.signal` is "The current abort signal, or undefined when the agent is not streaming" (`types.d.ts:235`), repeated in the tool execute signature `execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)` (`types.d.ts:372`). Docs are explicit: "Use `ctx.signal` for nested async work inside the handler. This lets Esc cancel model calls, `fetch()`, and other abort-aware operations started by the extension." (`docs/extensions.md:853`), and it is "usually `undefined` in idle or non-turn contexts such as session events, extension commands, and shortcuts fired while pi is idle" (`docs/extensions.md:1028-1029`). Scholar already threads it: `coordinator.loading.bindSignal(ctx.signal)` (`scholar/index.ts:141`) and `summarize`/review calls use `abortable(..., signal)` (`review-runtime.ts:296-299, 354-356`). Note the QA/test seam uses a hand-rolled registry: `new ModelRegistry({ complete: async ... })` (`tests/verify-scholar-figure-coverage.mjs:88`, `verify-scholar-learn-review.mjs:72`).

## Bottom line for the plan
- Spawning *real* subagents is not available from the SDK API; the only sanctioned route is `spawn("pi", ["--mode", "json", "-p", "--no-session", ...])` from inside the extension (as the shipped example does), which costs a cold process + re-discovery of extensions and does **not** share hooks/tools/state.
- Parallel **model** work *is* available today and already used by Scholar: `ctx.modelRegistry.complete(...)` / `provider.streamSimple(...)` fanned out through a bounded worker pool. Nothing in the SDK throttles those calls — Scholar's own `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6` is the only limit.
- Any new parallel path MUST thread `ctx.signal` (and Scholar's existing `abortable`/stall-timer pattern) and must handle `signal === undefined` in idle/command contexts.

## 1. VIEW — complete inventory

### 1a. TypeBox/params schema entries

- `tool-contract.ts:141` — `page: Type.Optional(Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })),` (the ONLY param `view` reads today; `read` shares it via startPage/endPage at :139-140).
- `tool-contract.ts:221-240` — `ToolDetails` carries `page?`, `bytes?`, `width?`, `height?` consumed by the view result.
- No maxItems on `page`; the multi-page precedent for an upper bound is `MAX_TOOL_PAGES = 12` at `tool-contract.ts:6` (enforced only by `read`, `source.ts:25`).

### 1b. Controller call site
- `tool-controller.ts:590-607` — `if (params.action === "view") { ... }`.
  - `:591-593` computes `canCapture` (Exam `status === "draft"` / Tutor `status === "active"`).
  - `:594` `const target = canCapture ? createFigureCaptureTarget(...) : undefined;`
  - `:595` `return await handleSourceView(book, session, params, recordOutlineValidationView, mutateBook, target ? async (page, width, height) => {...} : undefined);`
  - `:596-606` the `recordSourceFigureView` callback: reloads book, `target.assertCurrent`, `assertFreshSource` twice, clears/repopulates `sourceFigureViews`.
- `tool-controller.ts:133` — `const sourceFigureViews = new Map<number, SourceFigureView>();` (per-page memory receipt).
- `tool-controller.ts:603-605` — clear-on-activation-change + `sourceFigureViews.set(page, { activation, identity, page, width, height })`.
- `tool-controller.ts:1031` — `sourceFigureViews.clear();` on reset.
- Import sites: `tool-controller.ts:63` (`handleSourceView`), `:68-69` (`handleSnapshot`, `handleModeSnapshot`).

### 1c. Per-page side effects (in order)
`tool-actions/source.ts:89-134` (`handleSourceView`):
1. `:97-98` `if (!page) throw new Error("Scholar view requires page.");`
2. `:99` `assertPagesInModeScope(book, session.mode, session.recordId, page, page);`
3. `:100` `const rendered = await renderPdfPage(book, page);`
4. `:101` `await recordSourceFigureView?.(page, rendered.width, rendered.height);` — feeds the controller map (1b).
5. `:102` `recordOutlineValidationView(book, page);` — impl at `tool-controller.ts:277-282`: `if (session.mode || !isProvisionalOutline(book)) return; ... if (run?.checkpoints.some(checkpoint => checkpoint.page === page)) run.viewedPages.add(page);`
6. `:103-115` Learn `figureCoverage.viewed` mutation:
   - `:107` `const previousView = target?.figureCoverage?.pages.find((item) => item.page === page)?.viewed;`
   - `:108-109` gate `target && page >= target.startPage && page <= target.endPage && (previousView?.width !== rendered.width || previousView.height !== rendered.height)`
   - `:110-113` `mutateBook(...)` with stale-section guard `if (!section || page < section.startPage || page > section.endPage) throw new Error("The active Learn section changed while viewing its source.");` then `recordLearnView(section, page, rendered.width, rendered.height)`.
   - `recordLearnView` impl: `figure-coverage.ts:109-117` (creates `{page, read:false, candidates:[]}` entry if absent, sets `entry.viewed = { width, height }`).

🔎 Evidence is in. Direct answers first, then one scope decision for the plan.

**Is review in all modes now?** Yes — Learn (lesson crew + every question), Tutor (explanation + every question), Exam (the frozen form, every question inside that pass, at `exam_build`). Grading is deliberately not reviewed.

**Why a 12-page section feels endless** — measured on your own interrupted run of *1.2 Differential Calculus* (pages 32–43, **20 topics**): the pass planned `source 3 + teaching 21 + visual ≥14` ≈ **38–45 packets**, and the crew runs **6 at a time** → ~7 waves; 26 requests finished in the 8.6 min before it was interrupted. The cause is structural, not the model: `planReviewAssignments` emits **one visual packet per math/figure topic** and **one teaching packet per topic**, so long sections multiply packets. Author-side, `view` (1 page/call) and `snapshot` (1 rect/call) are also strictly sequential — ~N+F turns before writing starts.

**And no, we can't bolt on subagents**: pi 0.85.1's extension API exposes **no spawn/subagent/model-call-of-its-own** — only `ctx.modelRegistry` (what the crew already uses) and `exec`/child_process (the shipped subagent example literally spawns a second `pi` process). So the honest levers are: pack the crew smarter, and let the author's tool calls run concurrently — which I verified is safe: siblings in one message run via `Promise.all` (pi-agent-core `agent-loop.js:372`), and the extension's book mutations are queued per (vault, book) (`book-service.ts:113`), so parallel `view`s can't lose receipts.

options.label: Balanced: repack the crew + parallel author calls
options.description: Pack visual review across topics (all 12 pages in ~2 packets instead of ~20) and group up to 4 consecutive topics per teaching packet (~6 instead of 21); widen source windows to 6 pages (2 instead of 3) = ~10 packets ≈ 2 waves (~4x fewer). Plus: question reviews stop driving read-tool loops and inspect their grounded pages in one request (2–3 requests → 1), and the Learn instructions tell the author to fire independent view/snapshot/read calls together so pages render in parallel instead of N sequential turns. # Learn section loading and review speedup

Slug: `learn-load-speedup`

## Context

Loading a new Learn section takes too long. Measured on the user's real interrupted run of *Griffiths E&M / 1.2 Differential Calculus* (PDF pages 32–43 = 12 pages, 20 `###` topics, math in most topics): the review pass planned `source 3 + teaching 21 + visual ≥14` ≈ 38–45 packets, the crew runs `REVIEW_CONCURRENCY = 6` packets at a time, so the pass needed ~7 waves; 26 requests finished in the 8.6 min before the user cancelled it. Author-side, `view` (1 page/call, `tool-actions/source.ts:89`) and `snapshot` (1 rectangle/call, `tool-actions/visuals.ts:49`) are strictly one unit per call, so a 12-page section costs ~12 sequential view turns plus one turn per figure before any writing starts.

Intended end state: the same evidence is inspected by the same three reviewer roles under the same gates and receipts, but the pass runs ~2 waves instead of ~7 (packets ~45 → ~10), each question review costs one model request instead of a 2–3 request tool loop, and the author can render pages concurrently. Review coverage per mode stays as shipped: Learn = lesson crew + every question; Tutor = explanation + every question; Exam = the frozen form (all questions inside that pass). Grading is not reviewed.

Verified host facts the plan relies on:
- pi 0.85.1 runs sibling tool calls from ONE assistant message concurrently (`Promise.all`, `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js:372`), with no per-message cap; a tool opts out only via `executionMode: "sequential"` (Scholar declares none).
- Scholar's book mutations are queued per (vault, bookId) and each queued mutation reloads state (`book-service.ts:113-166`), so concurrent `view`/`snapshot` calls cannot lose receipts.
- pi's extension API exposes no subagent/model API of its own (only `ctx.modelRegistry`); the reviewer crew already is the extension's parallel fan-out. No new agent infrastructure is possible or needed.

## Approach

### Step 1 — `learn-review.ts`: pack visual review across topics

`planReviewAssignments` (lines 97–168) currently runs `for (const topic of topics) … pack(topic, pages, topicCrops)` (line 148), so every math/figure topic flushes its own packet. Replace the per-topic flush with a greedy multi-topic packer; keep the existing `pack()` filler (lines 133–147) and its crop-travels-with-its-page flush rule byte-identical.

1. Change `pack`'s first parameter from `topic: Topic | undefined` to `topics: Topic[]`, and store `topics` on each packet object instead of `topic`.
2. Build units in topic order:
   `const units = topics.flatMap(topic => { const topicCrops = crops.filter(crop => topic.cropIds.includes(crop.id)), math = topic.markdown.includes("$$"); if (!topicCrops.length && !math) return []; return [{ topics: [topic], pages: sorted([...topicCrops.map(crop => crop.page), ...(math ? topic.pages : [])]), crops: topicCrops }]; });`
3. Merge units greedily while the combined image count (`pages.length + crops.length`) stays `≤ visualPacketImages`, then `pack(group.topics, sorted(group.pages), sortedCrops)` per group. Preserve page order; crops keep their topic order.
4. Keep the trailing loose packet exactly as today: `pack([], sorted([...pages.filter(page => !viewed.has(page)), ...loose.map(crop => crop.page)]), loose)` (line 154).
5. Packet rendering (lines 155–166): for `packet.topics.length`, the instruction becomes `Crew assignment: figures and equations for topic(s) "A", "B" (pages 1, 4, 5). Compare the listed full pages and crops with each topic's captions, explanations and Key equation callouts. Other crew members review the other topics and pages.` and the payload becomes `{ topics: packet.topics.map(({ heading, markdown }) => ({ heading, markdown })), figures: packet.crops }`. The loose packet keeps its current instruction and `{ pages, figureInventory, figures }` payload. Ids stay `visual:${index + 1}`.

Invariants that must hold for any section (assert them): every section page appears in **exactly one** visual packet's `views`; every current crop appears in **exactly one** packet's `cropIds` and its page is in that packet's `views`; every packet holds `views.length + cropIds.length ≤ 6`; no packet is empty. Baseline for the observed shape (12 pages, 20 math topics, crops on 5 pages): 21 packets → 2.

### Step 2 — `learn-review.ts`: group teaching topic checks

Add `const TEACHING_TOPICS_PER_PACKET = 4;` beside `SOURCE_WINDOW_PAGES`/`VISUAL_PACKET_IMAGES` (lines 62–63). `SOURCE_WINDOW_PAGES` stays 4 (4-page fidelity windows are a review property, not a bottleneck).

Replace `topics.forEach((topic, index) => add("teaching", \`teaching:${index + 1}\`, …))` (line 124) with a loop over consecutive slices of 4:

- id stays `teaching:${sliceIndex + 1}`.
- instruction: `Crew assignment: topics ${first + 1}-${last + 1} of ${topics.length}, "A", "B", "C", "D". Review only these topics' explanations against their source pages; the outline shows where they sit, and earlier topics may already define terms. The objective check plan and whole-lesson flow are reviewed by a separate coherence check.`
- `reads`: sorted union of the group's topic pages.
- payload: `{ topics: group.map((topic, offset) => ({ index: first + offset + 1, heading: topic.heading, markdown: topic.markdown })), checklist: group.flatMap(topic => topic.coverage) }`.

The coherence packet (line 126) stays byte-identical, including its `teaching:coherence` id and `{ checks, requiredChecks, recap, keyPoints, checklist, keyEquations }` payload. Baseline: 20 topics → 5 grouped packets + 1 coherence = 6 (was 21).

### Step 3 — `review-layer.ts`: question reviews inspect prepared evidence

`reviewTargetQuestion` (lines 582–616) currently runs `reviewOne(reviewOpts, "assessment", { value, sourcePages })` without `prepared`, so the assessment reviewer gets the `read_source`/`view_source`/`view_crop` tools and spends 2–3 sequential requests per question (observed in the current verifiers). Add `prepared: true` to the `reviewOpts` object it passes, keeping `sourcePages`, the retry-once behavior, and both error strings unchanged.

Consequence to accept and state in the code comment: the reviewer inspects exactly the question's declared `sourcePages` (plus crops on those pages for vision models) — it can no longer pull adjacent pages. `assertQuestionGrounding` already requires those pages to be in scope. The prepared collector inside `reviewOne` (lines 338–360) fills `read`/`viewed`/`cropped`, so the existing "Reviewer did not read page N" guard still enforces completeness.

### Step 4 — `policies.ts`: let the author's independent calls run together

In `learnInstructions`, the source-preparation bullet (line 103, starting `- During initial source preparation…`) gains this sentence, and the bullets keep their order (views → crops → inventory), because a crop needs the canvas dimensions its `view` returned:

`Issue independent source calls together in one message — up to four \`read\`/\`view\` calls for different pages at a time; the harness runs them concurrently and each still records its own durable receipt. Then issue the crops for the pages you just viewed together (up to four per message), then account for every page's visuals in one \`notes.figureReviews\` call.`

No code change: the controller tolerates concurrent calls, and `sourceFigureViews` is keyed per page. Do not instruct batching of calls that depend on another call's result (`snapshot` needs the `view` result's `canvasWidth`/`canvasHeight`).

### Step 5 — update the verifiers that pin the old packing
